Object initializer

csharp_new_line_before_members_in_object_initializers #

Put each member of an object initializer on its own line. ⚠ Observable, and masked rather than inert: this export sets skala_place_simple_initializer_on_single_line = true, which joins a short initializer whatever this key says. Lift that and it answers — and it answers with the polarity reversed and over two targets at once. At false the oracle writes new Thing { A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 } even under skala_place_simple_initializer_on_single_line = false AND wrap_object_and_collection_initializer_style = chop_always, so false here overrides both. ⚠ Blocked on the one mechanism the registry does not have: expands propagates a generalized key's value TEXT into the keys it names, so it can only reach targets whose domain — and whose polarity — is its own. Three keys need the same missing piece and none of them is a coverage gap: this one, csharp_space_between_parentheses and csharp_new_line_before_members_in_object_initializers. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified masked. The recorded mask is confirmed: at the export's skala_place_simple_initializer_on_single_line = true both engines are flat; lift it and the oracle produces two distinct outputs while Skala stays flat, so a single-key oracle glob would report INERT. ⚠ The unprefixed spelling IS read by the C# formatter — the blanket claim near PhaseOneOptions.cs ~1279 does not hold for this key.
